bindings.rule: One Beh_<group>.npy container per original experiment group; neural file uses original mname/datexp/blk; transform uses mname/datexp. Neural chunks concatenate along the neuron axis. No author object loader is executed.

Behavior dictionary key is mname_datexp_blk, with _stimtype appended when the optional field exists. Presence matters; absence is distinct from an empty string. All original typed fields and order are retained. This rule describes the selected notebook route, not every utility.

The interpolation cache uses only physical session identity. The paper describes two swap variants being separate observations within a shared session for unsupervised/naive mice. A cache name cannot certify condition-specific support; no duplicate record is discarded.

Canonical targets are obtained from the behavior container: behavior stim_id selects UniqWalls, which maps frame-level ft_WallID. Metadata-row stim_id is retained as a separate descriptor; equality with behavior stim_id is unknown.

bindings.qualification: Source label vocabulary only; not evidence that any record has complete benchmark class support.

bindings.rule: NaN meaning is field-specific. The notebook documents out-of-behavior trial identity and no-reward timing fields separately. It does not explain metadata stim_id NaNs. Preserve every typed scalar and IEEE bit pattern; no imputation, drop or substitution into the finite-only consumer.

Source routines index behavior vectors by the neural frame prefix and use positive movement plus corridor membership. ft_Pos is within-corridor position; ft_PosCum is cumulative. Existing consumer uses trial-local bins, not author cumulative interpolation. Actual frame correspondence and units remain unverified.
